messages:
mina: heads up - small but steady stream of tiny GPU pods Pending in eu-central-az-c this morning, started ~0400 UTC. pods wait 30-90s then either get requeued or evicted. looks like a label/annotation timing issue again. anyone tracing?

 t omas: yep, i saw the spike. sampling shows binds failing because scheduler sees node has no 'gpu-count' label even though kubelet later reports it.

 kube-bot: alert: scheduler.bind_failures increased x5 in eu-central-az-c (metric: scheduler.bind.fail_rate). affected pods: 18 (tiny-class).

 felix: paste of node-init sequence from a problematic node (warmpool-azc-72):

 ```
Apr 12 03:59:12 cloud-agent: instance provisioned
Apr 12 03:59:15 kubelet: hello: node add
Apr 12 03:59:18 scheduler-prober: saw NodeReady for warmpool-azc-72
Apr 12 04:00:02 label-agent: applying labels gpu-type=rtx, gpu-count=4 (elapsed=44s)
Apr 12 04:00:03 kubelet: NodeReady (full)
Apr 12 04:00:05 scheduler: PreBind: node labels missing
```

 mina: so label-agent is delayed ~40s. scheduler treats the earlier NodeReady signal as enough and proceeds — race.

 ops: quick workaround idea: scheduler should attempt a short label-wait when binding fails for gpu-scheduled pods instead of immediately failing and triggering eviction. e.g., sleep/poll up to 30s for label arrival.

 tomas: +1. prefer scheduler-side change first (less infra churn). also canary a small increase to prebind/bind timeout for tiny pods in the affected region.

 felix: sketch of scheduler change:
 ```
if bindError == MissingNodeLabels and podClass == tiny:
  for i in range(0, 6):
    if nodeHasLabels(node):
      retryBind()
      break
    sleep(5s)
```

 mina: sounds reasonable. but watch out: keeping pods pending longer increases chance of short-lived migrations if preemption happens mid-wait. need to gate by node being warmpool-backed only.

 ops: we can check node annotation warmpool=true. only apply label-wait for those nodes to limit risk.

 oncall: i've started a 5% config canary in eu-central for tiny podClass that bumps bindTimeout to 75s and flips scheduler label-wait on for warmpool nodes. monitoring: pending_p95, eviction_rate, migration_egress.

 kube-bot: canary: config/cny-azc-4322 created (targets: eu-central-az-c tiny-class 5%).

 tomas: also flagging cost impact: when tiny pods churn we see egress + short-lived GPU runtime billing on warm nodes; last month that pattern added ~80GB/hr across EU during similar incidents. don't let timeout go wild.

 mina: agreed. plan: 1) turn on scheduler label-wait for warmpool nodes (canary 5%) 2) 75s bindTimeout for tiny-class (same canary) 3) instrument new metrics: scheduler.label_waits.{attempts,succeeded,failed} and pending_eviction_delay. 4) follow up RFC to reorder node-init so label-agent finishes before we advertise readiness.

 felix: i've opened PR for scheduler label-wait (https://go/redux/pull/9001) and added metrics. It'll include a feature flag default-off.

 ops: i'll review PR quickly and coordinate canary ramp. oncall, keep an eye on eviction_rate and egress.

 oncall: ack. i'll watch for 2 hours and alert if migration_egress > +10% or eviction_rate increases.

 mina: thanks team. if canary looks good we roll to 50% then region-wide. will post results in this thread.
